meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want, feel like', paired with 'захотеться'.

examples.text: Самсоновы, ну вы очнитесь! Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: Samsonovs, come to your senses! I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mood, attitude' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С таким настроением, конечно, не будет.
examples.trans: With an attitude like that, of course there won't be.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get tired', paired with 'уставать'.

examples.trans: She is very tired after work.

examples.text: Самсон, я устал. Мне сегодня ещё в суд идти!
examples.trans: Samson, I'm tired. I still have to go to court today!

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to set off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to set off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning '(to) home, homeward', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are bright stars in the sky.

examples.text: Вот молодёжь, ничего не знают! Это же Лещенко! Звезда!
examples.trans: Young people these days, they don't know anything! That's Leshchenko! A star!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодняшний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('today's').

examples.trans: The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

examples.text: С сегодняшнего дня говорите мне только правду.
examples.trans: From today on, tell me only the truth.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'party' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Приводи её сегодня к Димону на вечеринку!
examples.trans: Bring her to Dimon's party tonight!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'строен'). Common masculine noun meaning 'arranged' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Но этот мир устроен очень хорошо.
examples.trans: But this world is arranged very well.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'nowhere', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's go'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.
All right, let's go to our room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be able, to manage', paired with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Соседи, привет! Слушай, дружок, дай свой телефон на минутку.
examples.trans: Hi, neighbours! Listen, buddy, lend me your phone for a minute.

examples.text: Слушай, дружок, дай свой телефон на минутку.
examples.trans: Listen, buddy, lend me your phone for a minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to perpetrate; to create
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to perpetrate; to create', paired with 'сотворить'.

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to touch', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: Всё, хорошо, я тебя выпущу! Только собаку не трогай!
examples.trans: All right, fine, I'll let you out! Just don't touch the dog!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
